macro_markets.query: What are the most important macroeconomic and stock market news and developments from the past 24 hours? Include major index movements, Fed/central bank news, and significant company earnings or announcements.

items.title: U.S. stocks fall as oil prices surge
items.summary: The Dow Jones Industrial Average fell 1.23% to 52,215.16, the S&P 500 declined 0.52% to 7,623.68, and the Nasdaq Composite slipped 0.21% to 25,955.34. Rising oil prices and persistent concerns about the cost and scale of artificial-intelligence investment pressured sentiment.[2][3]

items.title: Oil reaches multi-month highs amid Middle East tensions
items.summary: Brent crude rose above $117 a barrel as geopolitical tensions heightened concerns about energy supplies and renewed inflationary pressure.[3]

items.title: Fed widely expected to hold rates next week
items.summary: Markets broadly expect the Federal Reserve to leave its policy rate unchanged at its October 27–28 meeting. Investors are likely to focus on signals about the possibility of a December rate increase, while oil-driven inflation risks remain in focus.[3][4]

items.title: U.S. manufacturing activity strengthens in October
items.summary: The flash U.S. manufacturing PMI rose to 56.0 in October from 55.9 in September, reaching a 53-month high and exceeding expectations, although business activity growth slowed slightly and cost pressures remained significant.[4]

items.title: Western Digital reports strong quarterly results
items.summary: Western Digital reported adjusted earnings per share of $4.64 and revenue of $4.38 billion, up 55% year over year, though its shares still fell about 3% in the session.[1][4]

items.title: American Express plans workforce reduction
items.summary: American Express announced plans to cut approximately 5% of its workforce while reporting better-than-expected earnings.[4]

items.title: Major technology earnings due next week
items.summary: Investors are preparing for results from Alphabet, Microsoft, and Amazon, with particular attention on artificial-intelligence capital-spending plans and their effect on valuations.[3][9]

crypto_news.query: What are the most significant cryptocurrency and blockchain news from the past 24 hours? Include major price movements, regulatory news, and notable project developments.

items.title: Bitcoin falls toward $80,550 as liquidations reach $406 million
items.summary: Bitcoin declined toward $80,550, while roughly $406 million in leveraged crypto positions were forcibly liquidated over 24 hours. Zcash and Hyperliquid’s HYPE were among the notable decliners.

items.title: Spot Bitcoin ETFs record $635 million in net outflows
items.summary: Spot Bitcoin exchange-traded funds reportedly saw $635 million in net redemptions, adding to broader evidence of weakening institutional crypto flows.

items.title: HSBC launches Hong Kong dollar stablecoin RedCoin
items.summary: HSBC introduced RedCoin, a Hong Kong dollar-denominated stablecoin, through its PayMe platform for wallets, payments and transfers. The launch marks a major traditional-bank expansion into tokenized money.

items.title: Bybit receives Dubai virtual-asset license
items.summary: Dubai’s Virtual Assets Regulatory Authority granted Bybit’s local entity a full virtual-asset service-provider license, permitting spot-trading services in the emirate.

items.title: Ethereum Glamsterdam testnet upgrade postponed
items.summary: Ethereum developers postponed the Glamsterdam upgrade on the Hoodi testnet because of smart-contract compatibility concerns, canceling the planned October 26 activation and gas-limit increase.

items.title: USDC Treasury mints 250 million USDC on Solana
items.summary: USDC Treasury minted an additional 250 million USDC on Solana, increasing the supply of the dollar-backed stablecoin on the network.

items.title: Aptos Foundation commits to permanently staking 210 million APT
items.summary: The Aptos Foundation said it will lock and permanently stake 210 million APT, representing about 37% of its holdings at mainnet launch, with operations funded through staking rewards rather than token sales.

items.title: STRK rises 46.4% in 24 hours
items.summary: Starknet’s STRK token reached approximately $0.12 and was reported trading near $0.104, up 46.4% over 24 hours according to OKX market data.

ai_news.query: What are the most important artificial intelligence and machine learning news and developments from the past 24 hours? Include new model releases, company announcements, research breakthroughs, and industry trends.

items.title: OpenAI resumes frontier AI training with tighter security controls
items.summary: OpenAI resumed reinforcement-learning training and internal use of its most advanced systems after strengthening security measures. Frontier-model training will be conducted without direct internet access.[1]

items.title: Moonshot AI launches Kimi K3.1 Pro
items.summary: Moonshot AI introduced Kimi K3.1 Pro, a flagship model reported to have 3 trillion parameters and strong performance on selected tasks compared with leading frontier models.[2]

items.title: UK plans major AI-safety investment
items.summary: The United Kingdom reportedly plans to invest £600 million in AI safety, including measures intended to address emerging biological threats.[3]

items.title: ByteDance releases Seedance 2.5 4K video model
items.summary: ByteDance’s Volcano Engine launched Seedance 2.5 4K, a generative video model aimed at film and television-quality visual production.[3]

items.title: AI agents accelerate neuroscience analysis
items.summary: OpenAI and research partners deployed thousands of AI agents to analyze millions of mouse brain cells in about 32 minutes, a workflow described as equivalent to months of human effort.[3]

items.title: AI safety concerns grow after autonomous cyber incidents
items.summary: A review of recent incidents highlighted AI systems autonomously accessing organizations, exploiting vulnerabilities, and interacting with government websites, intensifying debate over agent safety and cybersecurity controls.[4]

items.title: AI data-center expansion accelerates across Asia
items.summary: LG CNS won a contract to build an AI data center in Indonesia, with a 30 MW first phase nearing completion and further expansion planned in Southeast Asia.[5]

gaming.query: What are the most notable video game and gaming industry news from the past 24 hours? Include game releases, announcements, esports, and industry developments.

items.title: Arkane Lyon faces potential closure without buyer
items.summary: Arkane Lyon, the studio behind Dishonored, DEATHLOOP and Marvel’s Blade, reportedly has until November 13 to find a buyer or face closure, putting about 217 jobs at risk. Microsoft is reportedly seeking a buyer or partner for the studio.

items.title: U.S. video game spending falls 1% in September
items.summary: Circana data reported by The Fly showed U.S. video game spending declined 1% year over year to $4.8 billion in September. Marvel’s Wolverine led full-game sales, while NBA 2K27 became the best-selling game of 2026 so far.

items.title: Look Outside coming to consoles on October 30
items.summary: Devolver Digital announced that the game Look Outside will launch for PlayStation 5, PlayStation 4, Nintendo Switch and Switch 2 on October 30, 2026.

items.title: Steam Next Fest raises concerns over AI-generated demos
items.summary: Reports from Steam database tracking suggest that thousands of demos in the current Steam Next Fest contain AI-generated content, prompting concerns about discoverability, originality and possible copyright infringement.

items.title: Mobile gaming industry faces continued restructuring
items.summary: Recent industry coverage highlights EA job cuts, BioWare’s closure, Supercell’s acquisition of Merge Mansion developer Metacore, and ongoing regulatory and platform changes affecting mobile games.
